1.title: High-Performing Storage
1.text: Welcome to Module six: High-Performing Storage. This module covers task statement three point one, the first task of Domain three, Design High-Performing Architectures, which carries twenty-four percent of the exam. You will match block, file and object storage to the workload, choose the right volume or file system for the performance needed, and bridge on-premises storage to the cloud.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do five things. Tell block, file and object storage apart, and match each to a use case. Choose the right E B S volume type for I O P S or throughput. Choose among E F S and the F S x family for shared file storage. Tune S three for request rate and latency. And use Storage Gateway for hybrid storage.

1.title: Case Check-In: Lantern and Loom Speeds Up Storage
1.text: Lantern and Loom has several storage needs. A database needs steady, high I O P S. Web servers in several zones must share one file area. Artists on Windows want ordinary file shares. And the warehouse systems need a bridge to cloud storage. Pick the storage type for each.

1.title: Block, File and Object Storage
1.text: Start with the three storage types. Block storage is a disk attached to one instance in one Availability Zone. That is Amazon E B S, or instance store, and it suits databases, boot volumes and low-latency I O. File storage is a shared file system that many servers mount. That is Amazon E F S or Amazon F S x, and it suits shared content, home directories and lift and shift. Object storage holds objects by key over an A P I. That is Amazon S three, and it suits images, backups, data lakes and static content. The figure shows the three cards. Exam tip: one server and a disk is block; many servers sharing files is file; internet-scale objects is S three.

1.title: Amazon EBS Volume Types
1.text: E B S has two classes. S S D volumes are for I O P S, and H D D volumes are for throughput. G P three, General Purpose S S D, suits most workloads, boot volumes and small databases, with up to eighty thousand I O P S and two thousand mebibytes per second. I O two Block Express is Provisioned I O P S S S D, for sub-millisecond latency and more than eighty thousand I O P S, with ninety-nine point nine nine nine percent durability, up to two hundred fifty-six thousand I O P S. S T one is throughput H D D for big data and logs, five hundred mebibytes per second, and not bootable. S C one is cold H D D at the lowest cost, not bootable. As of the fifth of November, twenty twenty-six, limits keep rising, so check the page. Exam tip: I O P S-heavy means S S D; throughput-heavy means H D D; beyond G P three, use Provisioned I O P S.

1.title: EBS Features and Instance Store
1.text: A few E B S features matter. A volume lives in one Availability Zone, so use snapshots to copy it elsewhere. Multi-Attach, on I O one and I O two, lets several instances use one volume. You can change a volume while it is in use. Instance store is different: it is disk on the host, very fast, but temporary. Its data is lost when the instance stops or terminates, so use it for caches, buffers and scratch data. Exam tip: data that must survive belongs on E B S; fast scratch space that can be lost belongs on instance store.

1.title: Amazon EFS
1.text: Amazon E F S is serverless, elastic N F S file storage. It grows and shrinks automatically, to petabytes. Thousands of clients can mount it at once, including E C two, containers and Lambda. Regional file systems store data across multiple Availability Zones, while One Zone uses a single zone. For performance mode, General Purpose is the default and the recommendation. For throughput, Elastic suits spiky workloads, Provisioned suits known needs, and Bursting scales with size. E F S is Linux only; Windows instances are not supported. Exam tip: shared Linux files across servers and zones means E F S with Elastic throughput.

1.title: Amazon FSx File Systems
1.text: Amazon F S x offers four file systems. F S x for Windows File Server uses S M B and Active Directory, with native Windows features, so choose it for Windows shares and applications. F S x for Lustre is a parallel file system with high throughput and S three integration, for H P C, machine learning and media processing. F S x for NetApp Ontap speaks N F S, S M B and i S C S I, with NetApp data management, so choose it for multi-protocol needs and NetApp migrations. F S x for Open Z F S offers N F S, snapshots and clones, for moving Z F S workloads. Exam tip: Windows and Active Directory means F S x for Windows; fast parallel compute means F S x for Lustre.

1.title: Amazon S3 Performance
1.text: S three scales automatically: at least three thousand five hundred write and five thousand five hundred read requests per second, per prefix. Add prefixes and parallel connections to go faster. Multipart upload and byte-range fetches speed up large objects. S three Transfer Acceleration speeds long-distance transfers over the CloudFront edge network. The figure shows parallel clients spreading across four prefixes. Add CloudFront or ElastiCache for faster repeat reads. And S three Express One Zone gives single-digit millisecond access, in one Availability Zone. As of the fifth of November, twenty twenty-six, check the current request rates. Exam tip: more requests per second means more prefixes and parallelism; the lowest latency is Express One Zone.

1.title: Hybrid Storage with AWS Storage Gateway
1.text: A W S Storage Gateway bridges on-premises systems to A W S storage. S three File Gateway presents N F S or S M B file shares and stores objects in S three, with a local cache. F S x File Gateway presents S M B access to a F S x for Windows file system. Volume Gateway presents i S C S I block volumes, either cached or stored, with snapshots. Tape Gateway presents a virtual tape library and archives to S three. As of the fifth of November, twenty twenty-six, check whether F S x File Gateway is open to new customers. Exam tip: on-premises apps that need S three as files use S three File Gateway.

1.title: Choosing Storage
1.text: Here is the chooser. A database volume with steady I O P S is E B S G P three, or I O two above eighty thousand I O P S. Shared Linux files across zones is E F S. Windows shares with Active Directory is F S x for Windows File Server. H P C scratch with S three data is F S x for Lustre. Internet-scale objects is S three, and the fastest object access is S three Express One Zone. Temporary host-local speed is instance store. And on-premises apps using cloud storage use Storage Gateway. Exam tip: name the access method first.

1.title: What the Exam Asks: High-Performing Storage
1.text: Here is what the exam asks about storage. Which storage type: block, file or object. Which E B S volume: G P three, I O two, S T one or S C one. Which shared file system: E F S or one of the F S x family. Which S three option: prefixes, Transfer Acceleration or Express One Zone. And which hybrid bridge: the Storage Gateway type. Exam tip: underline the performance word: I O P S, throughput, latency or scale.

1.title: Design Check: Lantern and Loom Speeds Up Storage
1.text: Here is the Design Check. Cover the right column and answer each row yourself. The database needs steady I O P S: E B S G P three, or I O two if beyond its limits. Web servers in three zones share files: Amazon E F S. Artists need Windows file shares: F S x for Windows File Server. Images grow without limit: Amazon S three. Image processing needs single-digit millisecond access: S three Express One Zone. Warehouse systems need N F S to cloud storage: S three File Gateway. And throwaway scratch data uses instance store.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. Block, file and object map to E B S, E F S and F S x, and S three. For E B S, S S D is for I O P S, H D D is for throughput, I O two is for the highest I O P S, and a volume lives in one zone. For shared files, E F S serves Linux, and F S x serves Windows, Lustre, Ontap and Open Z F S. S three scales by prefix and parallelism, and Express One Zone gives the lowest latency. And for hybrid, Storage Gateway bridges on-premises and A W S.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. Lantern and Loom's order database needs sustained performance of one hundred thousand I O P S, with consistent sub-millisecond latency. Which E B S volume type fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: Provisioned I O P S S S D, I O two Block Express. It supports up to two hundred fifty-six thousand I O P S with sub-millisecond latency. The H D D volumes are for throughput and cold data.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. Linux web servers in three Availability Zones must read and write the same set of files, and the capacity should grow automatically. Which storage fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: Amazon E F S, mounted by all the servers. It is a shared, elastic N F S file system. E B S volumes and instance store belong to one server, and S three is object storage.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. The design team at Lantern and Loom needs Windows file shares that use their Active Directory sign-in. Which service fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Amazon F S x for Windows File Server. It provides native S M B file shares that join Active Directory. E F S does not support Windows instances, and Tape Gateway is for archive.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. Select two. Which two statements about Amazon S three request performance are correct? The five options are on the screen. The answers are A and C. S three supports at least three thousand five hundred write and five thousand five hundred read requests per second per prefix, and more prefixes with parallel requests multiply the rate.

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. Warehouse applications on premises write files over N F S and need the data stored durably in Amazon S three, with a local cache for fast reads. Which service should the architect use? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: A W S Storage Gateway S three File Gateway. It presents file shares on premises and stores the files as S three objects, with a local cache.

1.title: Answers at a Glance
1.text: Here are all five answers. Question one: B. Question two: D. Question three: A. Question four: A and C. Question five: C. In Module seven, we choose high-performing and elastic compute.
